reviews.title: Beware of Pliability’s “free” trial!
reviews.text:
I signed up for a free trial and later discovered I’d been charged $25.19 every month for five months — $125.95 total.

During those five months, I never received or saw a single email from Pliability alerting me that my trial was ending or that my credit card was being charged month after month. I searched my Gmail thoroughly—nothing.

Pliability claims their system shows emails were sent. When I asked them to provide copies, they said they couldn’t produce them or even show me what those emails said.

I canceled immediately when I discovered the charges and asked for a refund or even a partial goodwill refund. They refused every request.

Yes, the recurring charge was disclosed in the signup process. I missed it. But a company converting a “free” trial into an ongoing paid subscription should make darn sure customers know they’re being charged—not quietly collect $25.19 month after month.

My $125.95 lesson: Be very careful with Pliability’s free trial and watch your credit-card statement.

reviews.title: New Improvements
reviews.text:
UPDATE: I previously wrote a review complaining about struggles I had with the app after an updated platform that actually made the app harder to use (see below). Today I received an email about a new feature that directly addressed one of my issues. The app now has a session generator that allows you to tailor a session to your needs. Thus far the feature looks promising, though with some limitations. I was able to generate a couple of sessions that met my needs perfectly. However, when I ended up with sessions that were not what I was looking for, I had to start all over. Once a session was generated, I couldn’t remove a specific exercise that I didn’t want to do or replace it with one I wanted (I was given specific replacement options, none of which I wanted). Still it’s a pretty cool feature that I think I’ll make good use of.

OLD REVIEW: I’ve had the app for a couple of years. Really liked it at first, but lately it’s been buggy (e.g., I currently can’t access any of my favorite workouts because the app shuts down as soon as I select the workout); the search engine is completely worthless (seriously, if I search for an exact title, that should be the FIRST workout that appears, not a random workout that happens to contain one of the search words somewhere in the description - often, if the title is generic enough, I’ll get 50 results and none of them are the workout I’m looking for); and the workouts are redundant (literally, some of the older “named” workouts are EXACTLY duplicated in some of the newer workouts, where the title started with a date). Finally, it would be nice if there was a better mix of movements in each workout / more “full body” workouts. Having 5 “leg day” - oriented workouts in a single week is ridiculous. Upper body needs way more attention. Overall, for the subscription price, I expect better.

reviews.title: 41 Months Duplicate Payments- REFUND REFUSED
reviews.text:
I used this service years ago when it was ROMWOD. I eventually stopped using it and believed that old membership was inactive. Later, after ROMWOD became Pliability, I wanted to use the service again. I was using a different email address by then and could not access my old account with my previous credentials, so I created a new Pliability account.

I recently discovered that the old account had apparently remained active and was continuing to bill me.

I contacted Pliability support, and to their credit they investigated it. Their own records confirmed that BOTH of my individual accounts were being billed simultaneously from December 2022 until May 2026 — 41 billing months.

I explained that I obviously had no reason to knowingly purchase two memberships for myself to the same service. The older account originated around the ROMWOD/Pliability transition, used my old email address, and was an account I had been unable to access. That was precisely why I created the newer account.

Pliability nevertheless refused to refund any of the duplicate payments, citing its no-refund policy and characterizing what I was requesting as a “goodwill refund.”

What makes that response particularly disappointing is the resolution they offered instead: 41 months of free future Pliability access — exactly the number of months they confirmed I had paid for two memberships simultaneously.

I had already cancelled Pliability because I no longer wanted the service. Giving me another 41 months of something I chose to cancel doesn’t reimburse the money I spent paying for two memberships at the same time.

I understand a no-refund policy when someone forgets to cancel a subscription or simply doesn’t use what they purchased. That’s not what happened here. Pliability itself confirmed that the same customer paid for two individual memberships simultaneously for 41 months.

I actually liked the product, which makes this experience even more disappointing. Companies are ultimately judged not only by their product but by how they handle unusual situations when something goes wrong. After 41 months of duplicate membership payments, I expected Pliability to recognize that this situation deserved more than simply pointing to a blanket no-refund policy.

I hope Pliability reconsiders.

UPDATE: After everything described above, I made one final request to Pliability to reconsider its decision based on the unusual circumstances and the fact that they themselves confirmed I had been paying for two memberships simultaneously for 41 months. Their entire response was: “Hi Jack, this is our final decision.”

Unfortunately, that confirms that Pliability considers 41 months of future access an adequate resolution for 41 months during which they confirmed I was simultaneously paying for two memberships.

I liked the product, but this experience completely changed my opinion of the company behind it. When a company confirms that one customer paid twice for the same individual service for 41 months, refuses to return any of those duplicate payments, and hides behind a blanket no-refund policy, it certainly gives the impression that keeping the money matters more than doing what is fair for the customer.

Their final response to my request for reconsideration — “Hi Jack, this is our final decision.” — only reinforced that impression.

reviews.title: Clear Notice Promised, Clear Notice Not Delivered
reviews.text:
UPDATE after Pliability responded to this review with a stock reply:

Pliability’s response sidesteps the issue. This isn’t about whether I “felt more clarification was needed.” Pliability’s own communications contain specific, documented inconsistencies.

I initially selected a 7-day trial and was later offered a 30-day trial after I hadn’t used the service. The subsequent renewal email did not provide an exact renewal date. It was sent May 26 at 11:00 PM and said my subscription would renew “in 35 days ()” with the actual date left blank. I canceled on June 30, the same day I was charged and less than 35 full days after that notice was sent.

I also still cannot access the annual subscription I was charged for. Pliability told me in writing that my access would be restored and that they would follow up. Neither has happened.

These aren’t requests for clarification. They are specific failures in Pliability’s communications and handling of my account that their response does not address.——
“Hi there, The plan, the price, the renewal date and the auto-renew terms are all shown at signup before checkout, along with a box confirming the exact amount and date of the first charge, looking at your account, a renewal reminder did go out ahead of the charge but we're sorry you felt more clarification was needed. Your feedback has been submitted over to the team." 
——-
Initial review:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but I think prospective customers should understand how Pliability handles its annual trial subscriptions.

I overlooked the end of my free trial and was charged nearly $200 for an annual subscription. I canceled immediately after discovering the charge and requested a one-time exception because I had never actually used the service.

Pliability denied the request based on its refund policy. While I was disappointed, what concerned me more was what I discovered afterward.

The company’s published policy states that subscribers receive clear notice before being charged. However, the emails I received were inconsistent. My welcome email identified one trial expiration date, while a later email stated my subscription would renew in 35 days but left the actual renewal date blank. I shared those emails with customer support and pointed out that they did not appear to match the company’s own stated policy regarding clear notice.

After providing that documentation, I never received a response.

The product itself may be excellent—I never had the opportunity to use it. My review is solely about the subscription experience, billing practices, and customer service.

My advice: if you try Pliability, set your own calendar reminder the day you sign up. Don’t rely solely on the company’s communications to tell you when your annual subscription will begin.

Following this experience, I found other mobility apps that better fit my needs at a fraction of the annual cost.

reviews.title: Questionable Business Practice
reviews.text:
I purchased their mat for my practice. When it arrived, I wasn’t happy with the quality at all. It seemed cheaply made with a thin rubber mat as the top layer, and styrofoam padding underneath which was exposed, which made me feel like it wouldn’t take long to peel. This mat cost $150, which is as much if not more than a premium yoga mat. 

While I was technically able to return it, they said they weren’t responsible for shipping costs to return. I had no problem until I realized that return shipping would cost me at least $100. I asked if they had another option, which they did not.  I explained that I was unhappy with the mat, but it also made no sense for me to pay shipping costs that were as much as the mat itself. They offered me a complimentary 3 month membership of their app to make things right. I then asked for a 6 month membership to at least cover the majority of my loss on the mat. But they stuck to their 3 month offer, which I eventually declined and let them know I’d look to find another company to business with.

As much as I wanted to do this program, that whole experience didn’t seem fair, and I wouldn’t feel right supporting them any further.

reviews.title: Remember to Cancel Your Recurring Subscription – Not Legally Required to Warn In Some States
reviews.text: In some locations, it’s not legally required for an app company to alert you when your recurring payment is coming due since they are not providing a physical service – they can hide behind the fact that they provide software. Where I live, there is a bill going through the approval process to close this loophole, but it’s not yet law. I tried to get a refund a day after my subscription renewed when I noticed the pending charge on my credit card. I thought this would be easy as I had a good experience with this in the past the one time I’ve had to deal with other app’s auto renewals. However, Pliability instead continued to use the fact that the current law doesn’t cover their app and the new bill hasn’t gone into law yet rather than just refunding me. Is this legally correct? Sure. Is it good customer service? No. In fact, it feels like pretty sleazy business practice to me.

reviews.title: Zero Star (read the fine print)
reviews.text:
If I could give zero stars I would, solely based on the refund policy and customer service. The company does not offer refunds and digging though the refund policy/contract that is signed, the company (based on your state) must give you an email within 35 days before renewal. I live in a state where it is law that the company must give you an email notifying you of the renewal. I emailed customer service about this to get a refund because I no longer wanted to use the service, the representative randomly said a state and said I lived there. I corrected them notifying them of my actual state of residence, and then the representative said that the state does not require a notification email of renewal services. A two second search showed that they were wrong and the state does require a written notification before renewal. 

The company needs a refund policy, not refunding someone the same day the were charged is crazy!!. If I could write a review without giving stars I would. Customer service is everything and for that reason I am giving the app/company ZERO stars!!

I attempted to find a number to actually speak to a person and all I could do is find an email to the customer service department. I strongly recommend reading through everything and making sure if you cancel your service send a request via email and verify they cancel your account.

reviews.title: Too much clutter
reviews.text:
Your app used to be really good because it was simple and straight to the point for mobility work. Now it feels like you’re doing way too much. There are random workout plans mixed into what’s supposed to be a stretching and mobility app.

I don’t want workout programs. I only want mobility guidance. It feels like the app is constantly trying to push extra features and workouts in my face, and now it’s overwhelming, confusing, and harder to navigate. I can’t easily find the mobility content I originally paid for anymore.

I pay for this app specifically for mobility. I already have my lifting routine dialed in. I already have my cardio routine set up. The only reason I subscribed was to have guided mobility work. That should remain the main focus.

Please simplify the experience and make mobility easier to access again instead of burying it under unrelated workout content.

Why hyrox is even in the app blows my mind.

reviews.title: Awful
reviews.text:
I had a very disappointing experience with Pliability. I originally signed up for a 6-month subscription, but after realizing I wasn’t using the app, I deleted it—assuming that meant my subscription was canceled.
Unfortunately, I was charged again for another 6 months without any warning. When I reached out to customer service, I explained the situation clearly and requested a refund since I had not been using the app and had no intention of continuing. They refused to issue any refund.
This feels extremely misleading. Many users reasonably assume that deleting an app cancels the service, or at the very least expect a renewal reminder before being charged again. The lack of flexibility or understanding from their support team was frustrating and disappointing.
Be very careful when signing up—make sure you manually cancel your subscription, because simply deleting the app is not enough, and they will not work with you if you’re charged unexpectedly.

reviews.title: Not the stretching type
reviews.text: I’m a very active athlete who bounces between endurance (cycling) and CrossFit. I’ve found my limitations are from lack of mobility. While I’m relatively new at this I’ve already seen better movements and more flexibility. Definitely recommend.

reviews.title: I Now Love to Stretch
reviews.text: I absolutely love this app. The mobility test gives you a program to follow. I like that you can select longer or shorter daily sessions. The music and instruction are great. Worth the money!

reviews.title: Timely
reviews.text: Everything about this app is exactly what I needed + could ask for. This is one of those “I usually don’t write reviews” moments but felt compelled based on the intentionality that is evident that they’ve put into it. Do yourself and your body (and mind) a favor and spend some time with it, I’m certain you’ll find value (and then some) in it.

reviews.title: Pliability for LIFE
reviews.text: This is the only app you need to stretch and see improvements. It’s tailored to your needs, there’s a mobility test, it’s challenging to hold the stretches but also has the option for a quick stretch when you’re short on time. This has helped me improve as an older 40+ athlete all around.
